deepdive.sec: Private Tertiary Care Hospitals & Integrated Health Systems

bull_bear.body: Net cash position INR 5,906cr; Operating cash flow INR 7,144cr (FY26). Final dividend INR 0.50/share (25% of face value). Strategy favors internal accruals + project-specific debt for greenfield; active M&A/O&M exploration (recent Indore acquisition) for inorganic growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Competitive intensity in Gurugram (2 new competitor hospitals opening soon) potentially impacting doctor retention/pricing; 2) Slower-than-expected Noida ramp-up (occupancy ~30% vs breakeven ~40-45%); 3) Geopolitical tensions affecting Middle East patient inflows; 4) Regulatory delays in greenfield projects (Mumbai, Pitampura).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and pragmatic; emphasized 'procedural capacity' over mere bed count as key growth lever; acknowledged wage inflation but highlighted operational efficiencies (ALOS reduced to 3.04 days); reiterated discipline in M&A and strong clinical value proposition to retain talent.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly shifted narrative from 'bed occupancy' to 'procedural throughput' (OTs, Cath labs) as the primary constraint and growth driver, noting ALOS reduction (3.76 days in FY22 to 3.04 in FY26) masks true volume growth. Noida's early hiring of senior clinicians was framed as a deliberate P&L hit to secure long-term clinical depth, differentiating its ramp-up from pandemic-era launches (Lucknow/Patna).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The only stated funding philosophy is for growth capex: total capex of ~INR 48,500 million over five years "to be funded by combination of Debt funding and internal accruals" — no dividend policy, leverage target or return threshold is disclosed.
- Expansion is being pursued capital-light in places: Pitampura via a signed O&M agreement to jointly build, operate and manage; Varanasi under a built-to-suit and lease arrangement with a developer; South Delhi in partnership with DLF; and the Indore Cancer Unit via a business transfer agreement.
- The deck shows finance costs of INR 267 million and depreciation of INR 690 million in Q1 FY27 (vs INR 138 million and INR 451 million in Q1 FY26), but discloses no balance-sheet, net-debt or cash-flow statement.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Mature (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi): Rev INR 7,257cr (+11% YoY), EBITDA INR 1,935cr (+15% YoY, 26.7% margin). Developing ex-Noida (Lucknow, Patna): Rev INR 3,728cr (+33% YoY), EBITDA INR 1,207cr (+42% YoY, 32.4% margin). Noida: Rev INR 525cr, EBITDA loss INR 236cr (improving from INR 320cr in Q3), occupancy ~30%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Competitor hospitals opening in Gurugram may trigger a 'war for talent' and pricing pressure, but Medanta's scale and clinical depth act as a moat. | Global Health Limited | beneficiary | High | Management confirmed zero senior clinician attrition to date despite competitor announcements; procedural complexity and brand trust (Newsweek #1 in India) likely to consolidate market share rather than dilute it. |
| Noida ramp-up slower than initial hopes (30% occupancy) delays consolidated margin expansion. | Global Health Limited | loser | Med | While Q4 losses narrowed, breakeven pushed to H2FY27; however, the addition of high-margin specialties (transplants, obstetrics) in FY27 could accelerate the trajectory beyond linear occupancy assumptions. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as "one of the largest private multi-specialty tertiary care providers operating in the North and East regions of India" with key specialties in cardiac science, neurosciences, oncology, digestive and hepatobiliary sciences, orthopedics, liver transplant, and kidney and urology, per a CRISIL report titled "An assessment of the healthcare delivery market in India, September 2022".
- Claims the "Largest private hospital beds in operation under one roof in Delhi (NCR), Uttar Pradesh and Bihar"; Gurugram is called the largest single-location private hospital with operational bed capacity of 1,440, Lucknow the largest private hospital in Uttar Pradesh (planned 950) and Patna the largest private hospital in Patna (planned 650).
- Founded by Dr. Naresh Trehan (Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri, Dr. B.C. Roy Award); the deck frames the moat as "an ecosystem of excellence" of world-leading clinicians, state-of-the-art equipment, best-in-class infrastructure and research, under the philosophy 'Har Ek Jaan Anmol'.
- The stated growth model rests on six pillars: Bed Expansion, Attract Best Talent, Enhance Capabilities, Technology Advancement, Continuity of Care, and Thought Leadership.
- Ownership history noted: Carlyle (Anant Investments) bought a minority stake in 2013 and "exited completely in the IPO"; Temasek bought a minority stake in January 2015; GHL listed on BSE and NSE on 16th November 2022.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Indore Cancer Unit — an 80-bed cancer hospital being added under a business transfer agreement, announced April 2026, to be operationalized in Q2/Q3 FY27.
- [Regulatory] A revision in National Building Code (NBC) norms allowed Guwahati's planned bed capacity to be increased from 400 to 650 beds, and lifted that project's stated capex to INR 9,700 million.
- [Approvals pending] The Mumbai project awaits MHADA and Environmental Clearance, though additional FSI and Chief Fire Officer approval have been received.
- [One-off / group restructuring] Q1 FY26 carried a non-recurring exceptional income of INR 196 million, primarily due to reversal of a potential interest liability on EPCG following transfer of the EPCG license from MHPL to GHL — a base effect the deck flags for PBT and PAT comparisons.
- [Clinical proof points] Q1 FY27 firsts cited include Medanta Lucknow crossing 1,000 robotic joint replacement surgeries within one year of program launch and becoming the first private institution in Uttar Pradesh to perform a Whole Lung Lavage; Medanta Patna performed its first Transarterial Chemoembolization.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Mature margins compressed slightly (40bps FY26) due to employee cost inflation, offset by material cost optimization. Q4 mature margins recovered to 26.7% (+100bps YoY). Corporate overhead fully allocated to Gurugram. Management confident in sustaining 24-25% mature margin range via scale benefits and tariff hikes (CGHS full-year impact).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Double-digit growth expected driven by volume & realization; Margin: Mature units stable at 24-25%, Developing units (ex-Noida) >30%; Order Inflow: Strong international funnel activation; Capex/Commissioning: INR 45,000cr over 5 years for 2,700 new beds; Noida breakeven expected in H2FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Pipeline includes 400-bed Varanasi (build-to-suit), 400-bed Guwahati (land acquired), South Delhi (diaphragm wall complete), Mumbai & Pitampura (regulatory stage). Total planned addition: ~2,700 beds via 5 greenfield projects over 3-4 years plus ~500 beds via brownfield expansion.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Specialty gaps closure in Noida (Pediatrics, Obstetrics, Liver Transplant) and Patna (Lung Transplant, Chest Surgery); 2) Procedural capacity addition (10 new OTs across network including Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna); 3) International market recovery (Middle East, Bangladesh) + new markets (Africa, CIS, SE Asia); 4) Oncology expansion in Indore (80-bed acquisition).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Medanta delivered record Q4FY26 revenue (INR 11,958cr, +25% YoY) and PAT (INR 1,417cr, +40% YoY), driven by robust volume growth and improving realizations, while Noida losses narrowed significantly (INR 236cr in Q4 vs INR 320cr in Q3) signaling an inflection point toward breakeven in H2FY27. The strategic pivot from pure bed-addition to high-throughput procedural capacity (10 new OTs planned) and specialty gaps (oncology, transplants) underpins sustained ARPOB growth and margin resilience despite competitive intensity in Gurugram.
